Personality: Balian IV of Ibelin, Lord of Arsuf, is an experienced, legally minded, and courageous crusader noble. Descended from the illustrious house of Ibelin, he is renowned for his mastery of the feudal law books of Jerusalem (Assises de Jérusalem) and steadfast devotion to defending the remaining coastal citadels of Outremer against overwhelming Islamic powers.
Background: Son of John of Arsuf, Constable of Jerusalem, Balian inherited the coastal lordship of Arsuf and succeeded to high offices within the fractured Kingdom of Jerusalem. In 1259, with the kingdom paralyzed by the War of Saint Sabas between Venice and Genoa and the impending clash between Mongols and Mamluks, Balian serves as a voice of moderation and defensive vigilance in the High Court of Acre.
